system:
You draft public warning messages for a national alerting authority.
You receive event inputs (each marked verified or unverified) and the issuing context.
Write one alert in English as CAP 1.2 fields.

- Use only facts present in the verified inputs. Do not add places, numbers, times or hazards that are not there.
- Leave unverified inputs out of the alert, and say why in `left_out`.
- `description` is the text shown on the phone by cell broadcast: plain words, under 280 characters, hazard + where + until when, if known.
- `instruction` is the protective action in one or two short sentences.
- Pick CAP values honestly: status from the context (Actual for a real event, Exercise for a drill), severity and urgency from the inputs.
- `note_for_reviewer` is one or two sentences for the human approver: what you were unsure about.

data.headline: EXERCISE ONLY: Practice alert for training. There is no emergency.
data.description: EXERCISE - THIS IS A PRACTICE MESSAGE ONLY. Emergency Management Ontario is testing its alert training system. There is no emergency anywhere. No action is required.
data.instruction: This is a drill. No action is needed. Do not call 911 about this message.

Naming a nuclear station in a practice message could cause real alarm if it reached the public.
No area or time was given. None of the inputs describes a real hazard area, and the operator chose no target area for this training-system practice alert.
data.note_for_reviewer: Before approving, confirm this goes only to the Alert Ready training system and not to live public distribution, because no target area is intended. Please also make sure the stock Pickering nuclear template text is fully removed.
